newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: RESEARCH ALERT-VENEZUELA STOCKS KEPT OVERWEIGHT.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-VENEZUELA STOCKS KEPT OVERWEIGHT.

text.p: Morgan Stanley Dean Witter said it was maintaining its overweight recommendation on Venezuelan stocks despite a recent 12-hour national work stoppage.
- Morgan Stanley said Wednesday's strike would have no effect on the stock market in the short term.

- "We believe the market could return a further 20-30 percent in US$ in the coming 12 months and maintain our overweight position at five percent of our Latin American Model Portfolio versus a four percent MSCI-Latin America weight".
- Economist Carlos Janada estimates 4.0 percent overall GDP growth this year followed by 4.4 percent in 1998. "The non-oil economy is growing at around three to four percent and is accelerating".

- "Although economic reform is proceeding gradually, we think it will continue and expect to hear announcements regarding the privatization of steel company Sidor in coming months. We believe this will be interpreted positively by the market".

- 1998 presidential elections could be a source of market or foreign exchange instability. "Although we anticipate some nominal devaluation -- 10 percent for the rest of this year and 20 percent next -- this is factored into our expected return".

- Morgan Stanley said it held telephone company CANTV, electric utility Electricidad de Caracas and cement company Vencemos in its model portfolio. Electricidad was seen as a "strong buy" with a $2.00 target price.
